_about: Decision registry for the karpathy-jev router. identify: code picks candidate decisions for a moment from `moment` and `needs`. construct: one Jev request with the routing questions plus every candidate's questions, and only the state paths they declare. respond: code applies each decision's `gate` against the routing answers, then its thresholds; messages come from here. Thresholds are uncalibrated starting points: refit with `router.py replay`.

turn_start.does: Records the request and a git baseline. No decision.

before_command.does: Prepends `set -o pipefail;` to a piped command so the check's exit status, not the filter's, is observed. No decision.

before_first_edit.when: Before your first file edit of a turn.
before_first_edit.does: Routes the edit to the decisions below.

before_done.when: When you are about to end your turn after changing files.
before_done.does: Routes the turn's changes to the decisions below.

criteria.bug_fix: Something that should already work is broken.
criteria.new_behavior: Add or change a feature or behavior.
criteria.non_code: A question, explanation, documentation-only, or exploration request.
criteria.other: None of the above, or a mix.

instructions.question: How many materially different implementations could `request` reasonably mean?
instructions.material_difference: Two readings differ materially when they change which data is touched, what users observe, the scope of work, or its cost.

criteria.one_clear: One obvious implementation; a competent engineer would start without asking anything.
criteria.minor_variants: Only small details are open, and any sensible default would satisfy the requester.
criteria.several_material: At least two readings differ materially, and choosing wrongly would mean redoing the work.

assumptions_stated.instructions: Do `agent_said.messages_before_first_edit` name the interpretation of `request` the agent chose, or the assumptions it is making, or ask the user to choose?

true.means: The agent says in words which reading, scope, or assumptions it is going with, or asks.
true.example_shape: I'll read 'faster' as lower latency for single queries, not throughput; I'm assuming the index is the bottleneck.

false.means: The agent starts work without saying what it assumed.
does_not_count: A generic plan such as 'review, identify issues, improve, test'.

respond.message: The request has several materially different readings and you have not said which one you chose. Before editing, state your interpretation and assumptions, or ask the user.

instructions.question: Do the changes in `observed.hunks` add options, parameters, modes, or features that `request` did not ask for?
counts: Flags or parameters with no caller that needs them.
Caching, retries, notifications, or configurability nobody requested.

instructions.question: Do the changes in `observed.hunks` introduce a class hierarchy, interface, strategy, factory, or configuration layer that has only one concrete use?
instructions.does_not_count: A single plain function, or an abstraction the existing code already uses.

size_vs_need.instructions: How much of the code added in `observed.hunks` could be removed while still fully doing what `request` asks?
criteria: Nothing: every added line is needed for the requested behavior or its tests.
A few lines or one helper could be removed and the request would still be fully met.
Most of the added code could be removed and the request would still be fully met, for example a class hierarchy or configuration system where one short function would do.

respond.message: The change adds options, modes, or features the request did not ask for. Remove them.
The change adds an abstraction layer with a single use. Inline it.
Most of the added code is not needed for the request. Cut it down.

instructions.question: Does `observed.hunks[{i}].diff` change any line that `request` does not need?
counts_as_needed: Lines that implement the requested behavior.
Removing imports, variables, or functions that this same change made unused.

criteria.true: At least one changed line does not trace to the request.
criteria.false: Every changed line traces to the request.

unrequested_behavior.instructions: Does `observed.hunks[{i}].diff` change validation, logic, or behavior that `request` did not ask about?

style_edits.instructions: Does `observed.hunks[{i}].diff` change formatting, quote style, whitespace, comments, docstrings, or type hints on lines the request did not otherwise require changing?

restructures_working_code.instructions: Does `observed.hunks[{i}].diff` restructure or rename working code without the request needing it?

deletes_unrelated_code.instructions: Does `observed.hunks[{i}].diff` delete pre-existing code that `request` did not ask to remove and that this change did not make unused?

instructions.question: Is `observed.hunks[{i}].diff` an edit to documentation, a changelog, or release notes, when `request` does not ask for any documentation change?

criteria.true: The hunk edits docs, a changelog, or release notes, and `request` asks only for a code change. Count it even when the text describes the requested fix.
criteria.false: The hunk changes code or tests, or `request` asks for documentation.

respond.message: {file} ({hunk}): {reasons}. Revert what the request does not need; mention unrelated issues instead of fixing them.

gate.why: documentation-only or non-code requests need no test run

claims_done.instructions: Does `agent_said.final_message` claim that the task is finished, fixed, or working?

admits_unverified.instructions: Does `agent_said.final_message` state plainly that the change was not run, tested, or verified?

instructions.premise: `observed.commands_after_last_edit[{i}].command` ran after the agent's final edit; the end of its output is `observed.commands_after_last_edit[{i}].output`.
instructions.question: Does that command run a test or check that exercises the behavior `request` is about?
does_not_count: Listing files, git status, or printing file contents.
A linter or type checker, unless the request is about lint or types.

respond.if: claims_done >= 0.6 AND admits_unverified < 0.5 AND no command has (exercises >= 0.6 AND result = ok)
respond.message: You say the task is done, but no passing test or check that exercises the request ran after your last edit. Run one, or say plainly that it is unverified. A check piped into tail/head/grep reports the pipe's exit code, not the check's: run it plain.

gate.why: only bug fixes need a reproducing test

instructions.premise: `observed.commands_on_unfixed_code[{i}].command` ran while the fix was not in the tree (before any non-test file was edited, or after the change was stashed or reverted). Its result was `observed.commands_on_unfixed_code[{i}].result` and the end of its output is `observed.commands_on_unfixed_code[{i}].output`.
instructions.question: Judged on its own, ignoring what ran later: does that command run a test, script, or check that fails because of the problem `request` describes?
does_not_count: Listing files, reading code, git status, or searching.
A command that fails for an unrelated reason, such as a missing module or a typo.

criteria.true: The command exercises the function, file, or behavior that `request` names, and its failure is what the request describes. A pytest node, a test file, a doctest, or a one-off script of that behavior all count.
criteria.false: The command only reads, lists, or searches code, installs dependencies, or fails for an unrelated reason, or it does not touch the behavior `request` describes.

respond.if: no command on the unfixed code has (result = error AND reproduces >= 0.6)
respond.message: This is a bug fix, but no check failed on the unfixed code. Reproduce first: before editing any non-test file (adding a test first is fine), or with your change stashed or reverted, run a test or script that exits non-zero because of the bug, for example an assert; run it plain, not piped into tail/head/grep and not followed by echo. Then fix it and show that same check passing.

respond.if: no changed file is a test file (checked in code)
respond.message: This is a bug fix but no test file changed. Consider a test that reproduces the bug.

think_before_coding.title: Think before coding
think_before_coding.rule: Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.
think_before_coding.passes_when: Before the first edit, one or two lines name the reading you chose and what you assumed, or you ask. Unambiguous requests need nothing.
in_practice: If multiple interpretations exist, present them; don't pick silently.
If something is unclear, stop, name what is confusing, and ask.
not_checked: Whether a simpler approach exists and you said so.
Whether you pushed back when warranted.

simplicity_first.title: Simplicity first
simplicity_first.rule: Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.
simplicity_first.passes_when: The diff contains the requested behavior and its tests, and nothing a reviewer could delete without losing something that was asked for.
in_practice: No features beyond what was asked; no abstractions for single-use code.
No flexibility or configurability that wasn't requested.
If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
not_checked: Error handling for impossible scenarios (needs code context the diff lacks).

surgical_changes.title: Surgical changes
surgical_changes.rule: Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.
surgical_changes.passes_when: Every changed line traces to the request. Unrelated problems you noticed are mentioned in your message, not fixed.
in_practice: Don't improve adjacent code, comments, or formatting; match existing style.
Remove imports and functions your change made unused; leave pre-existing dead code alone unless asked.
not_checked: Whether you mentioned the unrelated issues you noticed.

goal_driven_execution.title: Goal-driven execution
goal_driven_execution.rule: Define success criteria. Loop until verified.
goal_driven_execution.passes_when: The last thing before you claim success is a passing run of a check that exercises the request, after your final edit. If you could not verify, say so plainly instead of claiming success.
in_practice: Turn the task into a verifiable goal: 'fix the bug' becomes 'write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass'.
For multi-step work, state a brief plan with a check for each step.
not_checked: Whether the test is a meaningful test of the fix rather than one written to pass.
Whether your plan's intermediate checks were run.
